mainTopic: אילא's fee for examining a בכור, and the ban on taking payment for judging, testifying, and the פרה אדומה service
overview: This amud begins with the end of a משנה about אילא in יבנה. The חכמים let him charge a fixed fee for checking a בכור: four איסרות for a small animal and six for a large one, whether the animal is תם or בעל מום. The גמרא explains that a large animal takes more work. It also explains that equal pay, given only once per animal, keeps anyone from suspecting him of a false ruling. A new משנה then rules that a judge or witness who takes payment has void rulings or testimony. Someone paid to sprinkle or mix the פרה אדומה water makes it plain water and ash. Only real losses may be repaid, such as food for a כהן who lost his תרומה, a donkey ride for an old man, and a lost day's wages. The גמרא learns from משה's words that תורה is taught for free, and a ברייתא adds 'buy the truth and do not sell it.' אביי then settles a contradiction from קידושין about מי חטאת, and the amud ends by explaining how the כהן could enter a rabbinic בית הפרס.

steps.title: The fee the חכמים allowed אילא in יבנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the example of אילא ביבנה, who was allowed a fixed fee for examining a בכור, paid whether the animal was תם or בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like אילא in יבנה, whom the חכמים (in יבנה) permitted to take four איסרות for a small animal and six for a large animal, whether it is unblemished or blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends its rule about experts who take pay for checking a בכור. It gives אילא ביבנה as the model of an expert whose paid rulings are still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, an expert who takes pay to examine a בכור is not trusted, because money could bias him. אילא was allowed a set fee that the חכמים themselves arranged. The fee is bigger for a large animal, and he is paid no matter what he finds.

keyTerms.meaning: Unblemished (may not be eaten as a בכור outside the מקדש)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base text. The rest of this passage asks why the fees differ and why he is paid even for a תם.

phrases.english: like Ila in Yavne,
phrases.notes: The end of the משנה's rule: an expert like him may take pay.

phrases.english: whom the Sages (in Yavne) permitted
to take four issars
for a small animal, and six for a large one,
whether unblemished or blemished.
phrases.notes: He is paid no matter what his ruling is.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: An approved expert may take a fixed fee for examining a בכור: four איסרות for a small animal and six for a large one, paid whether it is תם or בעל מום.

steps.title: Why the different prices?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a large animal costs six איסרות and a small animal only four.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks the reason for the price difference. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the first detail of the משנה: four versus six. It is a simple request for the reason, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why six for a large animal and four for a small one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the price difference in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the fee is higher for a large animal than for a small one.

steps.title: A large animal takes more work
steps.stepSummary: Checking a large animal takes more effort, so the fee is higher.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one involves great effort, and that one does not involve great effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the expert is paid by how much work he does. A large animal is harder to examine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Examining a large animal for a מום is more work, since it is bigger and harder to handle. So the fee is for his labor, not for his ruling itself.

phrases.english: This one (a large animal) involves great effort,
and that one (a small animal) does not involve great effort.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fee matches the amount of work. A large animal is harder to examine, so it costs more.

steps.title: Why is he paid for an unblemished animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that he is paid when he finds a מום, but asks why he is paid when the animal is תם.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Whether unblemished or blemished." Granted for a blemished animal, because he permits it. But an unblemished one, why?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second detail of the משנה and questions it. If he finds no blemish, the owner gains nothing, so why should he be paid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a בעל מום, the owner benefits because the expert permits the animal to be eaten. With a תם, the animal stays forbidden, so payment seems unjustified.

phrases.english: "Whether unblemished or blemished."
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the words of the משנה it is about to discuss.

phrases.english: Granted, a blemished one:
because he permits it,
but an unblemished one, why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second detail of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that he is paid even for a תם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pay makes sense only when the owner benefits. A תם gives the owner no benefit.

steps.title: Paying either way prevents suspicion
steps.stepSummary: If he were paid only for finding a מום, people would suspect he declares animals blemished just to get paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if so, people would come to suspect him and say: this "blemished" animal is really unblemished, and he permitted it only for the wage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that paying him either way protects his reputation and his honesty. He gains nothing by choosing one ruling over the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If pay came only with a ruling of מום, he would have a reason to invent blemishes. People would suspect him of permitting a real תם for money. Equal pay removes that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Because if so (if it were otherwise)

phrases.english: Because if so, they would come to suspect him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי: הַאי בַּעַל מוּם תָּם הוּא,
phrases.english: and say: this "blemished" animal is really unblemished,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי דְּקָא שָׁרֵי לֵיהּ — מִשּׁוּם אַגְרָא.
phrases.english: and the reason he permitted it is because of the wage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason for the rule (avoiding suspicion)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He should be paid only when his ruling helps the owner, that is, for a מום.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is paid for a תם too, so no one can say he invents blemishes to get paid.

steps.title: Couldn't people suspect him with an unblemished ruling too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that he could also be suspected of calling a real בעל מום a תם, so he can be paid again on a later visit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, about an unblemished one people will also say: it is blemished, and he did not permit it because he wants to collect his wage another time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Suspicion can still exist, just in the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he gets paid every time he examines, he might call an animal תם so the owner brings it back. Then he would earn a second fee when he later declares it blemished. So paying him either way does not remove all suspicion.

phrases.english: If so, about an unblemished one they will also say:
it is really blemished,
and the reason he did not permit it is that he figured

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלִשְׁקוֹל אַגְרֵיהּ זִימְנָא אַחֲרִיתִי!
phrases.english: so that he can collect his wage another time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that paying either way removes suspicion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The suspicion just flips: he might call a real blemish תם in order to be paid again later.

steps.title: He is paid only once per animal
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים set the fee for one examination only. Since there is no second payment, he has no reason to delay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן instituted payment for him once; they did not institute payment twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the expert gets paid only one time for each animal. So calling it תם cannot earn him a second fee.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying him either way blocks the suspicion that he invents blemishes. The one-payment limit blocks the suspicion that he hides blemishes. Together, his ruling cannot change his income at all.
steps.whatToRemember: The expert's pay is set so it never depends on his ruling. He is paid whether the animal is תם or בעל מום, and only once per animal. So he has no reason to rule either way falsely.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the חכמים built אילא's fee: the payment is fixed, equal for תם and בעל מום, and limited to one time per animal, so it cannot push his ruling in any direction. This is a special enactment for examining a בכור. The next משנה rules that a judge who takes payment has void rulings.

phrases.english: The Rabbis instituted payment for him once,

phrases.aramaic: תְּרֵי זִימְנֵי לָא תַּקִּינוּ לֵיה רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: they did not institute payment for him twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and closes the discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the scope of the enactment (one payment only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could gain a second fee by calling the animal תם and examining it again later.
steps.terutzMaskana: The enactment allows only one payment per animal, so there is no second fee to gain.

steps.title: Taking payment voids judging, testifying, and the purification process
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a judge or witness who is paid has void rulings or testimony. Someone paid to sprinkle or sanctify the פרה אדומה water produces plain water and plain ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who takes payment to judge has void rulings. Someone paid to testify has void testimony. Someone paid to sprinkle or to sanctify the purification water has made it ordinary cave water, and his ashes are just ordinary burnt ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three jobs where taking payment ruins the act itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The payment does more than create a sin. It cancels the legal power of the act. A paid judge's ruling has no force. A paid witness's testimony does not count. The paid person's מי חטאת lose their status and become plain cave water, and the ashes become ordinary ashes.

keyTerms.meaning: To sprinkle the פרה אדומה water on someone who is טמא מת
To sanctify the water by placing the פרה אדומה ashes into it
Cave water, meaning ordinary water with no purifying power
Plain burnt ashes from a fire

phrases.english: Mishnah
One who takes his wages to judge
his rulings are void
to testify, his testimonies are void
to sprinkle and to sanctify the purification water
his water is cave water
his ashes are plain burnt ashes

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing the examiner of a בכור, the משנה now states a general rule about taking pay for acts of מצוה and judgment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment for judging, testifying, or sprinkling and sanctifying makes the act void.

steps.title: Allowed compensation for real losses
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows a person to cover the actual losses of the one who serves him. This includes food for a כהן who became טמא and lost his תרומה, a donkey ride for an elderly man, and a worker's wage for the lost day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was a כהן and the person needing him made him impure, so he could not eat his תרומה, that person must feed him, give him drink, and give him oil to smear on himself. If he was elderly, the person must have him ride on a donkey. And he pays him his wages like a worker.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now explains what kind of compensation is still allowed, even though real payment is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is on being paid for the service itself. Paying back a genuine loss is a different matter. The כהן who cannot eat his תרומה gets replacement food. The old man gets transport. Everyone may be paid for the work he missed that day.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes him impure, so he cannot eat his תרומה
Gives him oil for smearing on the body
Has him ride on a donkey
Like a worker, meaning pay for the lost workday

steps.confusionAlert: "שְׂכָרוֹ כְּפוֹעֵל" does NOT mean he is being paid for judging or testifying. It only replaces the money he would have earned at his regular job that day. This is called שכר בטלה.

phrases.english: If he was a priest
and the person made him impure, keeping him from his teruma
he must feed him, give him drink, and give him oil to smear
And if he was elderly
he has him ride on a donkey
and he gives him his wages like a laborer

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This limits the ban in step 8 by allowing reimbursement of actual losses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Real losses such as food, transport, and a lost workday may be compensated. Payment for the service itself may not.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between payment for the service and payment for lost work (שכר בטלה) is the basis for how judges and rabbis are paid in הלכה.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a judge may not take payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these words derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's first rule. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question focuses on the judge who may not be paid. The גמרא expects a פסוק to be the basis.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: Gemara
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This asks for the scriptural source of the משנה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that forbids a judge from being paid.

steps.title: משה taught for free, so you must too
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, derives the rule from משה's words "ראה למדתי אתכם". Just as משה learned for free, the people learned from him for free, and they must pass it on for free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The verse says, "Behold, I have taught you..." Just as I learned for free, so too you learned for free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק. משה is saying that Torah is taught without payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Judging means applying תורה law, so it counts as teaching תורה. משה received the תורה from הקב"ה for free and gave it over for free. That sets the model for every later generation, so a judge cannot charge for his ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says
as the verse states
"Behold, I have taught you, etc."
just as I learned for free
so too, you learned for free

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דברים 4:5. משה taught תורה for free, so judging and teaching must also be free.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא makes the same derivation from the words "כאשר צוני ה' אלהי".
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught in a ברייתא: "As the Lord my God commanded me." Just as I learned for free, so too you learned for free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב's derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא points to a later phrase in the same פסוק, "as ה׳ commanded me." It shows that the Torah came to משה freely and must be passed on the same way. This confirms that רב's reading is an established teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: This is also taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita
"As the Lord my God commanded me"
just as I learned for free
so too, you learned for free

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This supports רב's derivation with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's teaching that Torah must be taught and judged for free.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on דברים 4:5, "כאשר צוני ה' אלהי".

steps.title: If no free teacher is available, pay to learn
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that if a person cannot find someone to teach him for free, he should pay to learn. It derives this from "אמת קנה".
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that if he cannot find someone to teach him for free, he should learn by paying? The verse says: "Buy the truth."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a new rule for the student's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on charging is on the teacher, not on the student. A student who cannot find a free teacher must still learn, even if it costs money. "Buy the truth" tells him to pay for תורה if he has to.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where is it derived that if he cannot find someone to teach for free
he should learn by paying?
The verse states: "Buy the truth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא moves from the teacher's duty to the student's duty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a person cannot find a free teacher, he must pay to learn תורה.

steps.title: Paying to learn does not allow charging to teach
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that someone who paid to learn may not say, "I paid, so I will charge." The פסוק says "buy the truth and do not sell it."
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he should not say, "Just as I learned it by paying, so I will teach it for payment"? The verse says: "Buy the truth and do not sell it."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes by blocking a logical excuse. Paying for your own learning does not give you the right to charge others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think he can earn back what he spent. The full פסוק says "buy" but also "do not sell," so the ban on teaching for pay stays in place. This brings the derivation full circle back to the משנה's rule that a judge may not be paid.
steps.whatToRemember: תורה teaching and judging must be free. A student should pay to learn if no free teacher exists. Even so, he may never sell תורה in turn. Only real losses, such as a lost workday, may be compensated.

phrases.english: And from where is it derived that he should not say:
Just as I learned it by paying
so too I will teach it for payment?
The verse states: "Buy the truth, and do not sell it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This limits step 13 so that paying to learn does not permit charging to teach.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תורה may be bought when necessary but never sold. Teaching and judging must remain free.

steps.title: Our משנה: paid sprinkling makes the water and ash worthless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה. If someone takes payment to sprinkle or to prepare the מי חטאת, the water becomes plain cave water and the ash becomes plain burnt ash.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he takes payment to sprinkle or to mix the ash into the water, his water counts as ordinary cave water and his ash counts as ordinary burnt ash.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from our משנה so that it can compare it with another source in the next step. This is a setup line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה continues the theme of steps 10–14: some מצוה work must be done for free. Here the rule is very strict. If the person takes payment, the פרה אדומה water and ash become invalid and are treated like ordinary water and ash.

keyTerms.meaning: To sprinkle the purifying water on a person who is טמא מת
Here: to 'sanctify' the water by putting the פרה אדומה ash into it
Plain cave water, with no special status
Plain burnt ash from a fire, with no special status

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה the word לְקַדֵּשׁ does NOT mean 'to marry.' It means mixing the פרה אדומה ash into the water. In the very next step the similar word הַמְקַדֵּשׁ DOES mean 'one who does קידושין (betrothal).' Keep the two meanings apart.

phrases.english: [One who takes payment] to sprinkle and to sanctify [the water] —
phrases.notes: 'To sanctify' here means putting the ash into the water.

phrases.english: his water is [like] cave water,
his ash is [like] ordinary burnt ash.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general ban on taking pay for judging and teaching to the specific case of the פרה אדומה water in our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment for sprinkling or mixing the מי חטאת makes the water and ash invalid.

steps.title: Contradiction from the משנה in קידושין
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in קידושין says a man can do קידושין using מי חטאת or אפר חטאת, even if he is a ישראל. This implies they have money value, which seems to clash with our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They pointed out a contradiction: if a man does קידושין with מי חטאת or with אפר חטאת, she is married. This is true even though he is a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different משנה that seems to say the opposite of our משנה. It now challenges the two sources to fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין only works with something worth money. So if מי חטאת can be used for קידושין, it must be fine to get value from them. Our משנה, however, seems to say that getting any value from them ruins them. The words 'even though he is a ישראל' make the point stronger: he is not a כהן or לוי, and the value still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they pointed out a contradiction' (one source is set against another)
Here: one who betroths a woman (does קידושין)
The purifying water of the פרה אדומה

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One who betroths [a woman] with purification water [or] with purification ash —
she is betrothed,
even though he is a [regular] Israelite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the משנה in קידושין against the line of our משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in our משנה that taking payment for מי חטאת makes them worthless.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קידושין requires something of money value. If מי חטאת can be used for קידושין, then benefiting from them must be allowed. That contradicts our משנה.

steps.title: אביי: two different kinds of payment
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה in קידושין is about the value of the work of bringing the ash and filling the water. Our משנה is about payment for the actual sprinkling and mixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is no problem. There (in קידושין), it is about payment for bringing [the ash] and filling [the water]. Here (in our משנה), it is about payment for sprinkling and for mixing [the ash into the water].
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. He shows that the two sources are talking about payment for different jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain labor of carrying the ash and drawing the water is not the מצוה act itself. A person may be paid for it, so its value can be used for קידושין. The actual מצוה acts, sprinkling and mixing the ash into the water, must be done for free. Taking pay for those acts is what ruins the water.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult' (the opening of an answer)
Filling (drawing the water into the container)

steps.whatToRemember: You may be paid for the hauling work around a מצוה, but not for doing the מצוה act itself.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult —
here [in Kiddushin] it is with the payment for bringing and filling,
here [in our mishna] it is payment for sprinkling and sanctifying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different kind of payment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be talking about the same value of the מי חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: קידושין works with the permitted value of bringing and filling. The ban in our משנה is on payment for sprinkling and mixing.

steps.title: The wording of both משניות supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the exact words fit אביי. Our משנה says 'to sprinkle and to sanctify,' which are the מצוה acts. The קידושין משנה says 'water' and 'ash' separately, meaning they are not yet mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise. Here it says 'to sprinkle and to sanctify.' There it says 'one who betroths with מי חטאת and with אפר חטאת.' Learn from this [that אביי is right].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support to אביי's answer by reading each משנה's wording closely. It then confirms with 'שמע מינה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה names the actions themselves: sprinkling and mixing. That fits a ban on payment for the מצוה act. The קידושין משנה lists water and ash as two separate items. That shows they have not been mixed yet, so the value involved is only the labor of bringing and filling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is also precise': the wording itself supports this reading
'Learn from it': the point is confirmed

phrases.english: It is also precise [in the wording],
for here it teaches 'to sprinkle and to sanctify,'
and there it teaches
'one who betroths with purification water and with purification ash,'
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer from the precise wording of both sources.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's split between payment for bringing and filling and payment for sprinkling and mixing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of our משנה ('to sprinkle and to sanctify') compared with the wording in קידושין ('water' and 'ash' listed separately).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The contradiction is resolved. Payment for the מצוה acts of sprinkling and mixing is forbidden. The value of bringing and filling is allowed.

steps.title: Our משנה: a כהן who loses his תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of our משנה. If the examiner, judge, or witness was a כהן and was made טמא so he could not eat his תרומה, he must be paid for that loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was a כהן, and [the person who needed him] made him טמא so that he could not eat his תרומה, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in our משנה. It quotes it only to set up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though payment for judging or testifying is forbidden, the משנה lets the כהן be paid back for a real loss. Because he became טמא, he cannot eat his תרומה, so he must be given food and drink instead. The quote stops at 'וכו' (etc.), because the גמרא is about to focus on one detail.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy food portion that only a כהן who is טהור may eat
'Etc.': the rest of the quote is left out

phrases.english: If he was a priest,
[and] he renders him impure from his teruma, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the פרה אדומה discussion to the next clause of our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who is made טמא while doing this work may be paid back for the תרומה he can no longer eat.

steps.title: How could the כהן go somewhere that would make him impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the כהן was allowed to go to a place where he would become טמא, since a כהן is forbidden to make himself טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he himself, how could he go [there]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the case in the משנה can even happen. A כהן is not allowed to become טמא מת, so how did he end up in that situation?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks as if the כהן lost his תרומה because he became טמא. But a כהן is forbidden to become טמא from a dead body. So the גמרא needs to explain how the כהן could go there without breaking that rule. The answer will come next.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה as saying the כהן was allowed to make himself טמא. That is exactly what the גמרא finds hard here.

phrases.english: He himself, how could he go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the case in the line just quoted can happen.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case in our משנה of a כהן who becomes טמא while acting as examiner, judge, or witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן is forbidden to make himself טמא מת. So the משנה's case seems to involve a forbidden act, and it is unclear how it could happen properly.

steps.title: The כהן went into a rabbinic בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 20. The כהן entered a בית הפרס, whose טומאה is only דרבנן, so he did not break a תורה prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went into a בית הפרס, which is only a rabbinic prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers how the כהן was allowed to go where he would become טמא. It says he went into a בית הפרס, which is forbidden to a כהן only by the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 20 assumed the כהן did something forbidden by going near טומאה. The answer shrinks the problem: the place was a בית הפרס, where a grave was plowed up and bones may be scattered, and its טומאה is only דרבנן. So entering there is not a real breach of the תורה law, and the רבנן were lenient about it, as the next step will show.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed over, so small bones may be scattered. It is treated as טמא by the רבנן.
Based on rabbinic law, not a direct תורה law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the כהן broke a law here. The point is that the place is only rabbinically טמא, so going there is allowed in the right way. Still, he can end up treated as טמא for eating his תרומה, and that is the loss the משנה says he must be paid for.

phrases.english: [He went] to a beit haperas, which is [only] rabbinic.
phrases.notes: Short answer that refers back to the question in step 20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the טומאה involved is only דרבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן seemed to have gone into real תורה-level טומאה, which is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: He entered a בית הפרס, whose prohibition is only דרבנן, so his going there can be allowed.

steps.title: רב allows blowing and walking through a בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the answer with רב יהודה quoting רב: a person may blow on the ground of a בית הפרס and walk through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: a person may blow [on the dust] in a בית הפרס and keep walking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that the רבנן were lenient about a בית הפרס. רב taught that a person may blow away the dust in front of him and walk through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing on the dust would uncover any bone hiding underneath, so the person can check his path step by step. Because a בית הפרס is only דרבנן, the רבנן accepted this simple check. This explains why the כהן was allowed to go there.

keyTerms.meaning: Blows (on the dust, to uncover any bones)

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן in our משנה went into a בית הפרס, which is only rabbinically טמא. The רבנן were lenient there (one may blow and walk), so his going was allowed. Yet he can still lose his תרומה, and he must be paid for that loss.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב's rule shows a general idea: when a טומאה is only דרבנן, the רבנן allow simple ways around it.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
phrases.notes: Attribution that introduces the supporting source.

phrases.english: A person may blow [on the dust of] a beit haperas and walk on.
phrases.notes: Blowing exposes any bone hidden under the dust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source showing why the answer in step 21 works.
steps.raayaObject: That a כהן may enter a rabbinic בית הפרס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב: מנפח אדם בית הפרס והולך.
